YHWH is written two ways in the same 2015 edition: Jonah has Evezøza (26×, the NT's word for the Lord, also in OT quotations, Act 7:49), Ruth has Yawe (18×, glossary-marked *Yawe in 1:6, though the NT glossary has no Yawe entry). 'the LORD God' = 'Evezøza, ndego Mbumbukiam' (JON 1:1, 4:6); 'the LORD his God' = 'Evezøza ..., tege Mbumbukiam' (JON 2:2); vocative 'Evézøza' (JON 1:14, 4:2). Until the Kuni team decides (question on names.md), draft with Evezøza (NT + Jonah) and say so in the chapter notes.
Ours was Neomi, built from the English pronunciation (letter:vowels). The human Ruth writes Naomi 33×, close to the spelling: for names the NT never uses, follow the spelling (see letter:vowels.2).

Ours was Eflata. 'Ephrathites' = 'Eflat khagua bawan-ák' (of the Ephrath clan; khagua bawan = clan, as NT 'Asa khagua bawan-ák', Luk 2:36); 'in Ephrathah' = 'Eflat khagua bawan mokho-te' (among the Ephrath clan). ph → f, r → l, th → t, final -ah drops.

Ours was Ngólam (the NT's 'Daughter' to the healed woman, Mrk 5:34), which Ruth/Jonah never use. The human says 'Sǽ-pakha.' 7× (sg) and 'Nogí sæ-pakha-za.' 2× (pl), the kin form with -pakha (feature kin_pakha). Naomi addresses her daughters-in-law as 'my daughters' with the same word.

Ours was bawan ezoqam. One's own people (kin group) = possessive + ezoqam: 'Qogi ezoqam, ndigu nogí ezoqam ndǿgoát' (your people will be my people, 1:16), 'ekeza ezoqam-té' (to her own people, 1:15). bawan = tribe, nation, descent group: 'niqa bawan' (2:11), 'Izlael bawan' (house of Israel, 4:11), 'teqa bawan-te' (among his brothers, 4:10), 'gekha bawan-âk' (of what people, JON 1:8).
Ours was ezoqa ndakinak. 'Young men' as a group = angana (men) ndakinak (3:10); in the harvest the young men are angana (2:9) or simply Boaz's workers, sasae ezoqam (2:15, 2:21).
The women who lived in that town; ours was 'sakheis, ndigu <X> avønin gimbo-puatat'.
Offspring = children (nakheis). 'The house of Perez' = 'Pelez-gi zi' (his line, as NT 'Zekop-gi zi', Luk 1:33). Ours was qazi (Rom 4:18).

'took the child and placed him on her lap' = 'took the child and held him close' (ngenøtam, the NT's stem for kissing/embracing). Ours was ava, which in Ruth/Jonah is a bag (RUT 2:17 'ava-te', JON 1:7 'ava-té').
'became a nurse to him' = 'she helped Ruth (with the child)': tøke (help) with noundape, whose meaning is not clear (only here). Ours was kewag (look after).
Boaz calls the other relative 'Khanánqa.' (Sir, as 'my lord' H113 in 2:13). Ours was 'Nǿfu.' (brother).

entries.source: קָנִיתִי לִי לְאִשָּׁה / I have acquired her as my wife
entries.note: 'she is now my wife' (nogu sævam, not zas). Ours was 'no ndugu no-okɨ́. Ndugu nogu zas ndǿgoát.' 'Mahlon's widow' = 'ngunuk ngæmam ... Malon gu-okɨam' (the widow Mahlon had married).

entries.source: יֻלַּד־בֵּן לְנָעֳמִי / a son has been born to Naomi
words: a son has been born to
entries.note: 'Now Ruth has borne a baby boy for her. He is as if Naomi's own child.' The human names the mother and adds 'andé' (as if). Ours was 'Nakhasam anganeam ndøqán, <X>-te.'

A blessing is 'Yawe zenda ndò꞉vé <X>-te' (may the LORD put his hand on X), 4× in Ruth; 3:10 'May the LORD bless you' = 'Yawe ndø̀goát qo namba' (be with you). Ours was khakheinøv (the NT's 'blessed is he'); in Ruth/Jonah khakhein means prepare, make (RUT 1:6 'gigiap vø̄khakheinam' got their things ready; JON 1:9 'gekhakheinam' made the sea and the land).

entries.source: בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַיהוָה / Blessed be he (by the LORD)
words: may he be blessed by the lord
entries.note: Ours was 'Mbumbukiam ngenek ezoqam bèkhakheinøvém' (Mat 21:9). The relative clause follows: 'te-te ndego qo geqatøke' (on him who noticed you, 2:19).

entries.source: בָּרוּךְ יְהוָה / Blessed be the LORD
entries.note: 'Joy (thanks) to the LORD, who has given you a grandson.' Ours was 'Evezøza-qa iz, yà beto-eqawát' (Luk 1:68). With Evezøza: 'Khanakhanákh Evezøza-te' (by rule).

entries.source: H2580 (favour; find favour in the eyes of)
words: in whose sight i may find favor
entries.note: 'find favour with X' = 'X has pity on me' (tanakh + go with -nø- me): 'Ezoqa nøme tanakh ndø̀nøgó' (someone will be kind to me, 2:2), 'qo tanakh kandambá qoqonøgo' (you have been very kind to me, 2:10); 2:13 'you have helped me much' (tøke). The question 'why have I found favour?' (2:10) becomes the statement 'I am a foreigner, but you have been very kind to me.' Ours was kuku (love).

Ruth renders human חֶסֶד as good deeds, matev mbomømboma (1:8, 3:10); 'May the LORD show you loving devotion' = 'Yawe matev mbomambaqape ndø̀matanám zo-te' (may he do good to you, 1:9). Jonah renders God's חֶסֶד as kuku matev (love, grace, JON 2:9, 4:2). tanakh (pity) is the human's word for favour and compassion (RUT 2:2, 2:10; JON 4:2 'ezoqam tanakh qozøgoatún' you are compassionate). Ours was tanakh matev (open); settles gap:chesed.
'you have comforted me and spoken kindly' = 'I am very glad that you have said this to me'. Ours was kha føgakh (strengthen). For 'relent' (JON 3:9, 4:2) see term:H5162relent.

entries.source: פָקַד יְהוָה אֶת־עַמּוֹ / the LORD had attended to his people
entries.note: 'the LORD has helped his own people again, with food' (tøke help, zø- them). Ours was '<God> ni-te tøke-qa ndowáv' (came to help, Luk 7:16).
See formula:the_lord_visited.h; ours was 'tøke-qa ndowáv'.

Bitterness of life = 'life is bad' (yage soqa): 'Noqa yage mø̀ndøsoqá' (my life has become bitter, 1:13); Mara is explained as 'Yage soqaín' (life is bad) and Naomi as 'Yage qanimāv' (life is good, 1:20). Ours was khaqain (bitter taste, Heb 12:15).
'there I will be buried' = 1sg future of otamb (bury); no passive is needed. Ours was 'manqei ozu' (grave, Act 2:29) in a nominal paraphrase.
'empty-handed' = 'with only (your) hands' (3:17). 'I went away full ... brought me back empty' = 'with husband and sons ... without husband, without children' (1:21). Ours was khakha-mbá.

entries.source: אַל־תָּבוֹאִי רֵיקָם / do not go back empty-handed
words: do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed
entries.note: Prohibitive of qavaq (go back) with the rising mark on the last vowel before -q. Ours was 'khakha-mbá nango ndø-òkho᷄'.

entries.source: H1481 / H1616 (sojourn, reside as a foreigner)
entries.note: 'went to reside in the land of Moab' = 'went to live in Moab' (yag, live). The foreigner status is not expressed. Ours was 'mo-manqei-aním mbá' (not of the land, Act 7:29).

entries.source: וַיְהִי רָעָב בָּאָרֶץ / there was a famine in the land
words: there was a famine in the land
entries.note: As Act 7:11. The human states the famine, explains it ('Zapa ndǿgo, Zuda manqei-te ndøgo, lou mbaín', because in Judah there was no food) and repeats 'Vikia sekeqape ndømát.' at the end of the verse. Ours was 'vikia seke ndøfakhán, ta manqei-te ndøgo'.
ndægó (singular copula) also after a plural number; ours was 'ndi꞉gú' (Luk 1:56).

entries.source: מִתְאַמֶּצֶת הִיא לָלֶכֶת / was determined to go
entries.note: 'Ruth had made up her mind to go with her' (matavap 'mind' + perfective). Ours was 'matavap āv genegó nqǽgo: ... Yaq kopømba mbaín, teqa matavap toqo-enend' (Luk 9:51).

entries.source: אֶל־אֲשֶׁר תֵּלְכִי אֵלֵךְ / wherever you go, I will go
entries.value: Qo ande āv khoqotéqāv, no ndǿgo tøtǿnáv
entries.note: 'wherever you go, I will go there' (ndǿgo there + 1sg future). Same frame for 'live' and 'die'. Ours was '... no até nøtaqá-pavát' (I will follow you, Luk 9:57).
'dip the bread in the yaf'; yaf is a local sauce or relish (only here). Ours was 'waen khaqain-qape' (sour wine, Jhn 19:29).
2sg imperative in a chain (vo-); stem afan. Ours was qoqom (Jhn 13:26).
No word for morsel: 'have some bread' = 'Lou qólóg' (eat food). Ours was 'lou mbewat'.
2sg imperative of log (eat) as a first command: qólóg. Ours was mòqológ (Jhn 4:31), which may be right as well.
'it (the food) filled her': qa- (it) + mbo- (her) + ewez. Confirms the stem; settles gap:satisfied.
Stem zivaz (put aside, keep): 'nøme sègeziváz' (she kept some back), 'guizivaz' (what she had kept). Ours was ivøvem (Jhn 6:12).
Ours was sunguz (Act 16:33). The human: 'Vø̀khæ-khakuám.' (wash your body).
'he put the barley on her head' (kawa head); the carrying is made concrete. Ours was 'nqanqa-té vø̄ve'.
Ours was qouz (Jhn 13:5, pour liquid); for grain the human has qoutaz.
'bring your other cloth'. 'The corner of your garment' (3:9) = 'ndabua khafuvam nonqo' (covering cloth, blanket; 3:4, 3:7, 3:9). Ours was 'ndabua qozaq nonqo'.

words: spread the corner of your garment over me
entries.note: 'take a little of your blanket and cover me' (khafu cover). Ours was gutav (Act 9:3). JON 2:4, 2:6 'ùnime꞉-gutambát' (the water closed over me).

Gleaning = picking up the left-over barley: 'bali khakhayakh ... pisam / pisum' (2:2, 2:3, 2:7, 2:15, 2:17, 2:22); 2:2 'bali khakhayakh ndigu, ezoqa tizuvatet, tæmǿpisám' (I will pick up the barley that the people drop); 'where did you glean?' = 'khae-tē qoqó-pisumam?' (2:19). Ours was 'bali nanga vingisam' (pluck heads, Mat 12:1).

The harvest is a season, viav: 'bali vingisam viav ndø-ogitát' (the barley-picking season began, 1:22), 'until the barley and wheat season was finished' (2:23). 1:22 adds an explanation in brackets: '(Bali ndigu loge gigiáp. Tiqa bugug andé eketóp.)' Ours was 'avøe gigiap' (open).

entries.source: קְצִיר הַשְּׂעֹרִים וּקְצִיר הַחִטִּים / the barley and wheat harvests
entries.value: bali nanga neka wit nanga viav
entries.note: See term:H7105.h. Ours was 'wit vingisam khøuwa'.
'the barley stalks they are tying up' (løvøtap + ab tie); 'among the sheaves' in 2:7 is left out. Ours was 'bali møvøyam' (open).
'the grain-threshing place' (tøkuza only in Ruth). Ours was 'bali evem nonqo' (built on Luk 3:17); evem (winnow) itself is confirmed: 'bali nanga ndø̀-evemét' (3:2).
'he lay down beside the heap of grain'. Ours was 'bali nqeitam' (built).

The human gives the weight in kilograms ('it was about 10 kilograms'), after 'she put it all in a bag (ava-te)'. For OT dry and liquid measures convert to kilograms / litres in the text. Ours was yakhav (basket, Luk 16:6).

entries.value: Taqa viniv andé áv 20 kilogrém ndægó
entries.note: 'its weight was about 20 kilograms' (viniv weight; BSB note 26 kg). Ours was 'bali yakhav siks'.

Ours was 'sasa ndøsømbiam' (the sleep stem sømbi). The human has buv in every case: 'temøbuv' (when he lies down), 'te꞉buv' (where he lies), 'sasa qóbūv' (lie down! 2sg), 'segebúv' (he lay down), 'sasa ndøbuv' (she lay down), 'gubuvam' (was lying), 'gubuvát' (she lay, 3:14), 'vøkhæbuvít' (lie here!); sleep = 'venanqei buv' (3:7 'venanqei gebuvat', JON 1:6 'venanqei mba ndoqobuvit'); JON 1:5 'gù꞉buvát'. Settles gap:lie_down_forms.

entries.source: וְיָדַעַתְּ אֶת־הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכַּב־שָׁם / note the place where he lies
entries.note: 'see well where he lies down'; locative relative ma ... ndøgo after the verb.

entries.source: עַד כַּלֹּתוֹ לֶאֱכֹל וְלִשְׁתּוֹת / until he has finished eating and drinking
entries.note: 3:3 'let him finish eating first' (optative); 3:7 'when Boaz had eaten' = 'Boaz lou gumulog ndøgo'. Drinking is left out both times.
Ours was khonoam-te (Act 16:37).
'about the middle of the night'. Ours was qamø-umba (Mat 25:6).

'fear took him' (nqova + ndaf take, mbo- him). 3:8 has 'Boaz tènesuzám. Yaq ma ge꞉qambun, nqova mbondáf.' (Boaz woke, turned over and was startled). Same idiom with zø- for the town in 1:19 ('was stirred'). Ours was 'kha wageap' (tremble).

entries.source: H2428 (אֵשֶׁת חַיִל, woman of noble character)
entries.note: 'a woman of good conduct'. Ours was 'sævam eqeieqeí'.
'a man of many goods, and famous' (iz-akhae). Ours was 'gigiap eve ezoqám'.

entries.source: אִם־דַּל וְאִם־עָשִׁיר / whether rich or poor
entries.value: Nøme gigiap kopoav ezoqám neka nøme gigiap-av ezoqám
entries.note: 'Some are rich men and some are poor men.' Ours was 'oskiá ndøgo, gigiap-av ezoqam o gigiap eve ezoqam'.

entries.source: H3190 (that it may be well with you)
words: it may be well with you
entries.note: 'so that you will live well'. Ours was 'eqeieqei qóyagát'.

words: seek a resting place for you
entries.note: The human makes the 'resting place' explicit: 'I will find you a husband' (3:1). Ours was 'pusup manqei'. The rhetorical 'should I not seek ...?' becomes a statement (gap:should_i_not.h).

alternatives.note: rest from work (Mat 11:28); RUT 2:7 'pusa-qase agé taeveáv' she did not rest even a little

entries.note: 'find rest in the home of your husband' = 'may he give you a good life with new husbands' (1:9). Ours was pusup (rest from toil, Mat 11:28), which stays right for physical rest ('pusa', RUT 2:7).

entries.source: מִי־אַתְּ בִּתִּי / How did it go, my daughter?
entries.note: 'My daughter, how did things go for you?' Ours was 'Gê, áv khané꞉go, qo-te?'. Settles gap:how_did_it_go.

entries.source: וַתַּגֶּד־לָהּ אֵת כָּל־אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה־לָהּ / told her all he had done
words: told her all that boaz had done
entries.note: 'told her the whole story, how well Boaz had treated her'. Ours was 'emanqat ate qægoam vømbō-vøndaz, av <X> gumbøe-matanam'.

entries.source: וַתַּעַשׂ כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר־צִוַּתָּה / did everything she had instructed
entries.note: 'she followed all the words her mother-in-law had said' (paev follow). For 'did so' after a command the human repeats the action verb: 3:15 'Lut ndabua vø̄vøndaz' (Ruth held the cloth out), 4:2 'yaq ndigu vø̄qonav' (and they sat down). Ours was 'sège-matanám'.

entries.source: כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאמְרִי אֶעֱשֶׂה / I will do whatever you say
entries.value: Gekha manqāt ndøgo, qo toqonø-ein, sǽmatanám
words: i will do everything you say
entries.note: 3:11 'whatever word you say to me, I will do it for you' (sǽ- 1sg future with 'you' object); 3:5 'Qanimáv. No matev ndæ̀matanám, av qonømbe-manqatat ndægo.' (Good. I will do as you told me). Ours had matēv and nøtaqá-matanám.

entries.source: וְהוּא יַגִּיד לָךְ אֵת אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשִׂין / he will tell you what to do
entries.value: qo ande gekha matev me qógō
words: he will explain to you what you should do
entries.note: 'Yaq manqat ndǿgo, tenøqá-eín, qo ande gekha matev me qógō' (he will tell you what you are to do). Ours was 'ndego ndø̀qa-eín, qo ande āv khoqotégō'.

entries.source: חַי־יְהוָה / as surely as the LORD lives
words: as surely as the lord lives
entries.note: An oath = a promise before the LORD's face: 'No Yawe-qá bugug-té qataqambø-manqaté, ...' (I promise you before the LORD, I will marry you). With Evezøza: 'No Evezøza-qá bugug-té ...' (by rule). Ours was 'no Evezøza-te, āv qaté-unimanqatín nqǽgo:'. Settles gap:oath_as_the_lord_lives.

entries.source: אַל־תִּוָּדְעִי לָאִישׁ / do not let the man know you are there
words: do not let the man know
do not let it be known
entries.note: The negative optative: be- + the prohibitive tone: 'Geté Boaz beqàme᷄kh.' (but let Boaz not see you), 'Ezoqa nøme betezø̀te᷄z av nqægo, ...' (let no one know that ..., 3:14); JON 3:7 'belòge᷄' (let them not eat). Feature negative_optative. Ours was the negative future 'mè꞉-otevák'.

entries.source: וַיִּקֶר מִקְרֶהָ / she happened to come to (the field of Boaz)
entries.note: Chance is rendered as not knowing: 'But she did not know that this field was Boaz's.' Ours was 'matev āv qanefakhán nqǽgo' (it turned out thus).

entries.source: הֻגֵּד הֻגַּד לִי / I have been made fully aware
words: i have been made fully aware
entries.note: 'I have heard the whole story (that ...)'. Ours was 'No <X>-qa yaq-te, manqat kandambá qæ-ewagam'.

entries.source: וַתֵּשֶׁב אֶת־חֲמוֹתָהּ / she lived with (her mother-in-law)
entries.note: Ours was 'namba gu꞉yagam'.
'Ruth clung to her' = 'Ruth stayed, with Naomi'; 'stayed close to the servant girls' = 'worked beside them' (2:23). Ours was 'gùmu-tøkenøvém' (built on Act 3:11).
'stay here with my servant girls' = 'sa nqánek, qoqógót, <X> namba' (be here); 2:21 'Até vøgó, nqanek <X> namba' (stay here with ...). Ours was 'namba mba qanøqóm'. Settles gap:stay_close.

Kisses are embraces: 1:14 'sège-møvøiú' (embraced, as the father in Luk 15:20), then 'ouo manqat vømbō-ein' (said goodbye); 1:9 'sègegavém' (held them, gavem seize/hold). Ours was 'sasa ndøngenøtam' (Mat 26:49), which the human uses for holding the child (4:16).
Prohibitive pl of khafen (drive away, Jhn 9:34): 'do not chase this girl away'. Ours was mivi (shame).
'Do not say a word to her about it' (prohibitive pl of ein). Ours was the built 'mbogùgu᷄'. Settles gap:rebuke_prohibitive.

entries.source: וַתִּפֹּל עַל־פָּנֶיהָ וַתִּשְׁתַּחוּ אָרְצָה / fell on her face, bowing to the ground
entries.note: 'she knelt (katuk knee) before him, bowed down, her head touching the ground' (khanaz touch). Ours came from Luk 5:12.

entries.source: וְלֹא יִפְגְּעוּ־בָךְ / so that nothing will happen to you
words: so that nothing will happen to you
entries.note: As a warning: 'But if you glean in another field, people may do bad things to you.' Ours was 'Soqaín ndøgo, matev soqa tømøqa-fakhan'.
A witness is one who has seen: 'zo ezoqa ewaqape ate nqazøte-qonøve, zo mòzoqeivím' (all you sitting here, you have seen it), 'Ni mø̀iqeivím' (we have seen). Ours was 'zøkeza bøí qazøte-qeivám'.

The human never uses the NT's nqovotaz in Ruth. The redeemer is the relative: 'Elimelek-ge ekeza ezoqam' (Elimelech's relative, 2:3, 4:1, 4:4, 4:8), 'nogé anganeam-pakha-gé ekeza ezoqám' (my husband's relative, 3:9). Redeeming the land = buying it, wi (4:4 'Manqei ndæ̀wí' I will buy the land, 4:6 'tæwi'); redeeming the widow = marrying her, okɨ (3:13 'beqakɨ́' let him marry you, 'ndæ̀qakɨ́' I will). The duty is explained once, from the law of Moses (2:20). 'Kinsman-redeemer' for the baby (4:14) = qazeo (grandson). nqovotaz may still fit God as redeemer (Isaiah, Psalms): question for the Kuni team.

entries.source: כִּי גֹאֵל אָתָּה / for you are a kinsman-redeemer
entries.note: See term:H1350.h. Ours was 'qo nigi ekeza ezoqám, ni nqovotaz-qa nqoqote꞉go'.

entries.source: יֵשׁ גֹּאֵל קָרוֹב מִמֶּנִּי / there is a redeemer nearer than I
entries.value: ndego uni qoge qøivis-pakha-ge ekeza ezoqam
entries.note: 'But there is another man; he is the true (uni) relative of your husband. Let him be asked first' (bàmbokho-beváp). Ours was 'Ndego qo-te avønín. Ndego no mø̀ndøløvú, taqa yaq-te'.

entries.source: <X> הוֹלִיד אֶת־<Y> / X was the father of Y
entries.note: The 2015 Ruth writes gemanaz, each link opened by Yaq; the newer NT (Mat 1) writes gendomanaz without Yaq. The first link has ndøqán (4:18). The heading 'These are the generations of Perez' = 'Deivid-qa zapa av nqǽgo qande-itán: Tege atanakha-zapa Peléz.' (David's line began thus: his ancestor was Perez). Which spelling for 1 Chronicles and Genesis: question for the Kuni team.
'Jonah, Amittai's son' (appositive, no ndego). With both parents: 'ndego Tama neka Zuda, tige yo' (whom Tamar and Judah had, their son). Ours was '<X>, ndego <Y>-gé yó. Tegu evo, <Z>.'

entries.source: וְיִקָּרֵא שְׁמוֹ / may his name become famous
entries.note: 'This man will be famous in Israel' (iz akhae, as 2:1 'iz-akhaé'); a wish: 'may your name be great' (4:11). Ours was '<X>-qa emanqat, <place>-te, bè-panqavøém'.
Ruth's form of YHWH (18×; glossary star in 1:6, but no glossary entry). Recorded for the divine-name question; the live drafting term is term:H3068.h (Evezøza, open).
Also the NT glossary (Mat 12:39). Jo- → Zio- (as Zion for John); vocative Zíona (4:4).
Double t simplified.

With the class noun taon (town): 'Niniva taon kandambaqape' (the great city); Ninevites = 'Niniva taon-ak' (3:5); the king of Nineveh = 'Niniva taon-ak-ge kawa' (3:6), 'Niniva kawa' (3:7). Glossary entry Niniva. NT Mat 12:41 'Niniva vemiav-ak', Luk 11:32 'Niniva ezoqám'.
r before a consonant drops, sh → s. Class noun taon (1:3) or manqei (4:2).
Jo- → Zio-, double p simplified; class noun taon. The NT (Acts 9-11) may spell Joppa differently: check before using it in Acts-related notes.
As the NT (Iblu, glossary Aleluya 'Iblu manqát').
Added by the human in 2:20 to explain the redeemer's duty (not in the Hebrew).

words: now the word of the lord came
entries.note: Both books open with 'Qàgoám.' (it happened / it was so) as a sentence of its own, before the time setting. Use it for a book (or a new story) that opens with וַיְהִי; not for every וַיְהִי.
Opens a scene; JON 1:1 adds it although the Hebrew has no 'one day'.

entries.source: בִּימֵי שְׁפֹט הַשֹּׁפְטִים / when the judges ruled
entries.value: manqa ovøyam megetapak Izlael manqei gimbo-kewagam
entries.note: 'In those days, when the law leaders looked after the land of Israel'; judge = 'manqa ovøyam megetapak' (leader of judgement).

entries.source: קוּם לֵךְ אֶל־<place> / Get up! Go to <place>
entries.note: 'Get up!' (קוּם) is not rendered before a command to go; the command is 'qonǿqáv' (go there!). Where 'get up' is the point: 'Mòqosuzám.' (wake up, get up, JON 1:6).

A reply takes the hither -ndo-/-ndu- frame: gundu-ein (she), gendo-ein (he), gindu-einim (they); to a group: guzø-qavøiu / gezø-qavøiu (answered them). Speaker first, then the frame verb, then the quote.
Also when a man speaks to a woman (gu- for the woman; feature verb_subject_prefix.2).
gezø-ein (he), guzø-ein (she) to several people.
Stem bevap (ask); pl bevøpém (JON 1:8, 1:11). The long frame 'āv ... nqǽgo' is common with questions.

Prayer = guligulim (NT 'pray'): 'āv gene-guligulím nqǽgo, “...”' (4:2); 'called to the LORD' = 'Evezøza-té genø-akhá' (2:2). Jonah's psalm opens with 'Geguligulim,' (he prayed) and is laid out as //1 poetry lines.

entries.source: וַיְהִי־עֶרֶב וַיְהִי־בֹקֶר / there was evening and there was morning
entries.note: 'When evening came, the morning dawned': 'qakhagus ndøgo' is always subordinate in the corpus (13 verses); 'qanaqanus qandopave' (Act 27:39, 10:23).

'(Now) it is the third day' (Luk 24:21). Gen 1: menas and siks by pattern, misika, foa (with -mbo-, Jhn 11:39), faev attested. The first day: 'Ndøgo bugukhokhof khøuwá.' (bugukhokhof first, Rev 8:7; predicate noun with final accent as Luk 23:54).
Naming with iz + name + mbo-akha (Mat 1:25). Gen 1:5 'Mbumbukiam waev, iz Khøuwa mbo-akhá' (God named the light Day).
khaiya = the visible sky (stars, weather: Heb 11:12, Mat 16:2-3); yan = heaven (God's dwelling; 'heavens and earth'). Gen 1:8 God names the khaiya 'Yan'. Lights and birds are 'khaiya-te'.
'the heavens and the earth' = 'yan neka manqei-qape' (Act 4:24, Rev 14:7). For רְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמַיִם use khaiya-te (term:H7549).
qatøzo = separate (Mat 25:32 the shepherd separates; Mrk 10:9 let no one separate). Past geqatøzo; optative beqatøzo (2x in the corpus).

entries.source: H8432 בְּתוֹךְ (in the midst of, between)
entries.note: livin-te = in the middle of (Act 12:6 Peter between two soldiers; Act 8:25 on the way).

entries.source: H8414 + H922 תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ (formless and void)
entries.note: khakhamba = empty, deserted (Act 1:20 'may his house be deserted'); 'void' as 'there was nothing' with mbaín.

entries.source: H2822 + עַל־פְּנֵי (darkness over the surface of)
entries.note: 'darkness covered (the land)' (Luk 23:44). Gen 1:2 'anana-mba-qape bøivun ndønqeivøém' (the deep = term:H8415).
løvuvav = fly (down) (Mrk 1:10, Mat 3:16: the Spirit like a dove). Gen 1:2 without the simile. Whether it can mean hovering in place: question for the Kuni team.

entries.source: H6960 קָוָה (be gathered; מִקְוֶה gathering of waters)
entries.note: pind = gather, assemble, said of people (gindupindam 22x). For the waters by analogy: 'manqei kopo-té bepindám', 'ibøkha gipindam ndøgo' (the water that gathered). See gap:waters_gather.h.
fakhan = come out, appear (Rev 12:1, 12:3 a sign appeared); optative befakhan (8x).

entries.source: H1877 / H3418 דֶּשֶׁא / יֶרֶק (vegetation, green plants)
entries.note: gagayag = grass, plants of the field (Mat 6:30, 1Pe 1:24).
avøe gigiap = crops (Jas 5:7; 2Co 9:10 'avøe khayam ezoqam' sower). 'seed-bearing' = 'nanga-us ndigu' (with seeds; -us by pattern).
nanga = fruit, seed; viam = bear (Jas 3:12, Jhn 12:24, Luk 6:43 géviamák). The first draft had an unattested ndiviam.
tae nanga = seed to sow (1Co 15:36); 'with seed in it' = 'ta nanga mokho-te ... tae nanga ndøugu' (inside, Act 10:12 'Ta mokho-te ndøugu').
'animals of all kinds' (Act 10:12; bugug form, vinivinimba different). After each class in Gen 1.

entries.source: H3974 מְאֹרֹת (lights; the greater and the lesser light)
entries.note: waev = light. Gen 1:16 names the two lights in the text (feature explicitation): 'Waev kandambaqape, ndøgo khøuwá ... waev khasøkhasis, ndøgo løvøyák' (sun, moon; Luk 21:25). Marked for the team.

entries.source: H4475 / H4910 / H7287 (rule, dominion, rule over)
entries.note: 'he will be king over them' (Luk 1:33). People over the animals (Gen 1:26, 28): 'ndigu / zo ... kawa zømbógoát'. The lights rule as a predicate noun: 'khøuwa-qá kawá' (the day's chief). See gap:rule_over.h.
umingiap = sign, wonder (83x). מוֹעֲדִים as 'pindap khøuwa' (feast days, Jhn 5:1); 'times and seasons' in the NT = 'khøuwa neka viav' (Act 1:7).
khaev = shine; 'let it shine' = betekháev (Mat 5:16), betøkháev (Luk 12:35).
No verb for swarming: 'let there be very many (living creatures) in the water' (kopoav-qape very many + begó).

entries.source: H5775 עוֹף (birds; winged birds, birds of the air)
entries.note: pipisi = bird; 'the ones that fly' = ndiløvuvam (Jas 3:7). 'birds of the air' = 'pipisi, khaiya-te'. 'let birds fly' = bete-løvuvat (by pattern; gap:birds_fly.h).
'big animals' + 'they go in the water' (Jas 3:7 creatures of the sea). Gen 1:21 as two sentences.
nanak = tame (Jhn 4:12 Jacob's livestock; Act 11:6 tame and wild animals).

entries.source: H7431 / H7430 רֶמֶשׂ / רֹמֵשׂ (creeping things, what crawls)
entries.note: visigiap = crawl (reptiles, Act 10:12, 11:6, Jas 3:7). 'that crawls on the earth' = 'manqei-qape-te ndivisigiap'.

entries.source: H2416 חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ (beasts of the earth)
entries.note: lozokhak = wild (Act 11:6 wild beasts; Luk 9:58 foxes).
'put his hand on them' (Heb 11:20 Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau). The wish form is 'zenda ndò꞉vé' (term:H1288.h).

entries.source: פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ / be fruitful and multiply
entries.note: No idiom found (gap:fruitful_multiply.h): 'become many' with the 2pl future as a command (Rev 14:7 'møe zógoát' fear God). 'let birds multiply' = 'pipisi ... kopoav begó'.
'live all over the earth' (image to meaning; 'all over the world' 1Pe 5:9, Act 24:5). The sea creatures: 'ndaola-te, ibøkha ate qægoam, zo zóyagát'.
'I put it into your hands' (Luk 4:6 'qoqá zenda-té qatǿvé'; Jhn 17:2). Recast from command to grant: mark for the team.
bugug = face, form; Christ, the image of God (2Co 4:4, Col 1:15). Gen 1:26-27 'andé niqa bugug me', 'andé ekeza bugug me', 'andé Mbumbukiam-qa bugug me'.
Hortative zí- (Jon 1:7 'let us write') + khakhein (make); zíkhakheinám is not in the corpus (gap:let_us_make.h). Who 'us' is stays open, as in the Hebrew.

entries.source: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה בָּרָא אֹתָם / male and female he created them
words: male and female he created them
entries.note: Mrk 10:6 quotes Gen 1:27; the human form is kept.

entries.source: הִנֵּה נָתַתִּי לָכֶם / Behold, I have given you
entries.note: Luk 10:19 'Behold, I have given you authority'. Gen 1:29-30.

entries.source: לָכֶם יִהְיֶה לְאָכְלָה / they will be yours for food
words: they will be yours for food
entries.note: Possessive + noun + ndǿgoát (will be), as Rut 1:16. lou = food.
tantáv = very (Rut 2:20; 46x). Gen 1:31 'Áe, ndøgo eqeieqei tantáv.' (Áe = behold in narrative, Rut 3:8).
ve = put (Eph 1:22). Gen 1:17 'Mbumbukiam ndigu khaiya-te genøvé'.

entries.source: וַיְהִי־עֶרֶב וַיְהִי־בֹקֶר / and there was evening, and there was morning
words: there was evening, and there was morning
entries.note: All six day-formulas of Gen 1 (1:5, 8, 13, 19, 23, 31) use this pair, not khagus / qanaqanus (our draft). qapøis = night falls, vøndōpave = day dawns. Ordinary "evening" stays khagus (GEN 19:1, 24:11, 29:23), "morning" qanaqanus (19:27, 20:8).

"Now the day has become the Nth": gè- + the numeral (menás 2, misiká 3, foá 4, fáev 5, síks 6). The first day is "Khøuwa qa-kopo, nqánek" (1:5). Not the NT's "khøuwa mø̀ndømø-N-éz" (Luk 24:21), which our draft used.

entries.source: H3117 יוֹם as daylight, opposite of night
entries.note: "God called the light Day" = iz "paveat" (1:5); daylight against lova (night) in 1:14, 1:16, 1:18 and "forty days and forty nights" = "paveat foti-a, lova foti" (7:4, 7:12). For "day" as a unit of time keep khøuwa (term:H3117). Our draft had khøuwa for the named Day.

alternatives.note: heaven as God's place: from heaven (GEN 19:24, 21:17, 22:11), God of heaven (24:3, 24:7), the gate of heaven (28:17): term:H8064heaven.g

entries.note: The created heavens and the visible sky are khaiya (29 verses in Gen 1-30); yan (8 verses) only where heaven is where God and the angels are. Our draft (term:H8064 yan) had it the other way for Gen 1:1.

entries.source: H8064 שָׁמַיִם as the place of God
entries.note: "from heaven" = yan-te ndo꞉go (21:17, 22:11, 22:15); "the gate of heaven" = yan-gí mboqóg (28:17); the ladder reaches yan (28:12).

entries.source: וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי־טוֹב / God saw that it was good
entries.value: Mbumbukiam āv geneqeív nqǽgo, ndøgo qanimáv.
words: god saw that it was good
saw that the light was good
entries.note: The perception frame "āv geneqeív nqǽgo" (he saw thus) + the content; "good" here is qanimáv (25 verses in Gen), not eqeieqei.
"And the thing happened thus" (1:7, 9, 11, 15, 24, 30). Our draft built "Yaq ate av-té qafakhan" from the NT.

Jussive of fakhan (appear, come about) with bete- (feature optative_bete): betéfakhan, plural beté-fakhanam; light "shines": Waev betékha, then "Yaq waev vø̄kha" (and there was light, 1:3). Not "<X> begó" (our draft).
The stem qat- (divide): purpose "tøqatatat" (to separate, 1:6, 1:14), jussive "betē-qatoat" (1:18), past "livin-mbá gunumu-qatá" (1:4). Not the NT geqatøzo.

"I swear it" = "Manqa mbusa nò-unimanqatintét" (21:24). manqa mbusa is also a promise (15:18, 24:7). Gen 47:31, 50:5 need it.

entries.source: וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ אָרְצָה / bowed low to the ground
entries.value: gèkhafutáv, tiqa megemege-te. Bugug até manqei-té.
entries.note: "he knelt before them, the face to the ground" (18:2, 19:1). Ruth "katuk gumø̀kuī" (formula:fell_on_her_face.h) is the woman's form. Gen 33:3, 37:7-10, 42:6, 43:26 need it.

entries.source: וַיַּשְׁכֵּם בַּבֹּקֶר / got up early in the morning
entries.note: "the next day dawned, early" (21:14, 22:3); "qanaqanus qandopave" (20:8); still dark "qanaqanus lovølova-ús" (19:27, 26:31; formula:early_still_dark). The verb "got up" (gesuzam) is often left out. Gen 28:18, 31:55 need it.
Greeting and family kiss in Genesis (27:26-27, 29:11, 29:13). Ruth's farewell kiss "sège-møvøiú" (1:9, 1:14) is for leave-taking only: use it for Gen 31:28, 31:55.

words: lifted up his voice and wept
entries.note: weep = vin- (gèvín he wept, vø̄vin chained); "aloud" = "his crying went up" (27:38). Many in Gen 33, 42-46, 50.

"in sleep-seeing": in a dream = venanqei tam-te (20:3, 20:6; MAT 1:20, 2:13 written venanqei-tam-te); "he dreamed" = "venanqei ndøtám" (28:12) and what he saw follows with "Yaq nqáe!". venanqei alone is sleep (also in "venanqei nonqo" of marital relations). Gen 37, 40-42 need "my dream", "dreams" (plural by context).

alternatives.note: the famine as a thing, 'food-lack matter' (26:1, 12:10 'lou lou-av matev qagoam ndøgo, ùnime꞉-soqá' the famine was severe)

entries.note: "a great hunger fell" (12:10, ACT 7:11 for Joseph's famine, RUT 1:1); the hunger of a person = ifin (25:32 "No ifin khàpe-nømbe-khouwév" I am famished). Gen 41-47 use it about 25 times: vary with lou lou-av matev as the team does.

alternatives.note: food: 'there was grain in Egypt' = 'Izip manqei-te, lou zua ndøgō' (there was food, ACT 7:12)

entries.note: "grain and new wine" = "wit neka waen" (27:28, 27:37). For the grain bought in Egypt (Gen 41-47) the NT's account of the same story says lou (ACT 7:12); heads of grain in Pharaoh's dream: "wit nanga" (JHN 12:24 kernel).
NT only (111 verses; Genesis 1-30 has no prison). "put in prison" = "ndimbula-te vø̄nqeitaz" (ACT 5:18); the jailer = "ndimbula keoge ezoqam" (ACT 16:23) for the warden of Gen 39:21-23.

entries.source: H5921 + H1004 אֲשֶׁר עַל־בֵּיתוֹ (steward, the man over his house)
entries.note: Abraham's chief servant "who managed all he owned" = "ekeza sasae kawa ezoqam ... teqa gigiap ate ndægo go꞉kawaevtam" (24:2); the NT manager "kewagám" (watched over all, LUK 16:1). Joseph over Potiphar's house (39:4) and Joseph's steward (43:16, 44:1) by these.

entries.source: H56 / H5594 / H1058 אָבַל / סָפַד / בָּכָה (mourn, lament, weep)
entries.note: "mourning and crying" (23:2 Abraham for Sarah; JON 3:5 mutøkhop for fasting grief). "the days of mourning for my father" are told as "my father will die soon" (27:41). Gen 37:34-35, 50:3-11 need it; weep: formula:wept_aloud.g.

alternatives.note: put in (the grave): 'ginø-otøvém' they buried him (25:9), 'tinø-otøvém' he was buried (25:10); Ruth 'tǽ-otambát' I will be buried (1:17)
a grave, burial place (23:4, 23:6, 23:9 'manqei pakha upøgim nonqo' a burial site)

entries.note: "carry (him) to the earth-hole" (23:4, 23:6, 23:19) or "put (him) in" with otøv- (25:9-10). Both stems are attested in Gen 23-25; the Ruth entry stands as the passive. Gen 35, 47:30, 49:29-31, 50 need it.

The NT tells Joseph's story with zapikia-za (ACT 7:13 "Zosef ekeza zapikia-za tènezømás" made himself known to his brothers). One brother: term:H251.g (eveqase). Addressing them "brothers!": Jacob to strangers "Nǿfuap" (29:4), so nøfu is the polite address, not kinship.
20 verses in Gen 1-30. Donkey = donki (12:16, 22:3), cattle = kao (12:16, 13:5), goats = naningus (27:9, 30:32), sheep = sip (term:H6629.g).
palai (13 verses in Gen 1-30); "tents" with khoev (house): palai khoev (13:5).
"God has judged my matter (in my favour)" (30:6, explained as the meaning of Dan). Gen 31:53, 49:16 need it.

alternatives.note: my father, and the vocative 'Tát!' (27:34, 27:38, 27:41; 19:31-34 the daughters of Lot: 'our father'); also God the Father in the NT

entries.note: A third person's father is eve with the possessor: tege eve (his, 25:19), tugé eve (hers, 29:12), "Lot-gé evé" (11:27), "qogu qavo-ge eve" (your mother's father, 28:2). tat (the NT form of term:H1) is "my/our father" and the address. mother = evo (21 verses; "qogu qavo" your mother, 28:2).

"male children": sons = nakhei angana (59 verses), daughters = nakhei sakheis / nakhei mbasi (term:H1323pl); one son = yo (term:H1121) or nakhasa anganeam (a male child, at birth). children = nakheis (30:3).

alternatives.note: kindness, grace (H2617 חֶסֶד: 24:27 'Teqa kuku matev'); kuku alone is the NT's love/grace
like (a taste): 'av no nqanømbe-khaneat' that I love (27:4)

entries.note: A man's love for a woman is poev ("Aezek poev kandambá, tu-te" 24:67; Jacob for Rachel 29:20, 29:30); "my husband will love me" = "Noge anganeam, poev ndakin ndǿvé, no-te" (29:32). Gen 37:3-4 (Israel loved Joseph) and 44:20 need it.
"I am God Almighty" = "No Mbumbukiam ndégo, Bazaføgakh-Qape" (17:1); "God Almighty" in a wish = "Mbumbukiam, ndego Bazaføgakh-Qape" (28:3). Gen 35:11, 43:14, 48:3, 49:25 need it.

entries.source: H5945 + H410 אֵל עֶלְיוֹן (God Most High)
entries.note: 14:18-22 (5 verses); NT the same.

Create and make are the same verb khakhein- (97 verses in Gen 1-30); with a plural or living object khakheinøv- (1:21, 1:27). "Creator of heaven and earth" = "ndego khaiya neka manqei-qape gekhakheinam" (14:19).

alternatives.note: land, country, ground, a place (363 verses): 'Keinan manqei' (the land of Canaan), term:H776

entries.note: The whole earth = manqei-qape; a land or the ground = manqei. "the families of the earth" = "bawabawan ate nqægo, manqei-qape-te nqago" (12:3).

words: offered it as a burnt offering
entries.note: "animal-burning act" (22:2-13); an offering in general = "etoam matev" (gift act, 4:3-5); altar = lou-qase (term:H4196). Gen 46:1 "offered sacrifices" = term:H2077.
Genesis gives the meaning in brackets after "iz <Y> mbo-akhá" (feature name_meaning_brackets), with a colon; Ruth inside the speech with ‘ ’. For Genesis use the brackets.
Gen 1:9-10 and the Red Sea crossing (HEB 11:29); Jonah's "dry land" as the shore is manqei-qape (term:H3004). The earth was dry = "manqei ùni-tønepáp" (8:14).

entries.value: aqon- (gu-aqonøvem she stole them; nø-aqonøvem I stole them)
entries.note: Rachel stole the household gods = Laisol … gu-aqonøvem (gen031, built on nø-aqonøvém with gu- for a woman). A thief = aqona ezoqam. 'stole the heart' (31:20, 26, 27) is deceive, term:H7411.g.

entries.value: khavoz- (qoqonømbe-khavoz you deceived me; gènømbe-khavozám he deceived me)
entries.note: Jacob to Laban (29:25) and Laban to Jacob (31:26-27) with the same verb; 'he deceived Laban' = Leiben gembøe-khavozám (gen031:20, built on the same pattern).

entries.value: pav- (follow): Zekop vømbō-pavat; heading Leiben, Zekop gembopavát
entries.note: Abram pursued the kings = gezøpavát (followed them, 14:14); 'hotly pursued me' (31:36) = nakhamas-té qoqonø-pavat (followed me quickly).

entries.source: H5381 הִשִּׂיג / H1692 הִדְבִּיק (overtake, catch up with)
entries.note: No verb 'overtake' in the corpus; 'arrived, reached' (møfakhan) with -te on the one reached (gen031:23, 25). The store's built 'gèmø-tøkenøvém' is 'cling' (gap:stay_close) and was not used.

entries.source: H5674 עָבַר (cross a river, go past)
entries.value: qantav- (Yuflatis kea ndøqantav; 'I will not go past this heap' = nóqantavák)
entries.note: Used for crossing the Euphrates (31:21) and for not passing the boundary stones (31:52, negative future nó-/qó-…-ák).

entries.value: su qogem- (cut the wool): sip su qogem-qa gewav (he went to shear the sheep)
entries.note: The NT's sheep before its shearers (ACT 8:32). Gen 38:12-13 (Judah's sheepshearers) need it.

entries.value: wi (buy and sell): ndego ni gèwí (he sold us)
entries.note: ACT 7:9 tells Joseph sold into Egypt with gèwiím; the same stem buys (GEN 23:19 gewi). Gen 37:27-28, 45:4-5 need it; who buys from whom is shown with -te.

entries.source: יִשְׁפֹּט יְהוָה בֵּינִי וּבֵינֶךָ (may the LORD judge between you and me)
entries.value: <God> segé-geveá, … eqeieqei gekha ezoqam ndǿmatanam, qô o nô
entries.note: Sarai's wish (16:5) is the model for 31:37 and 31:53 ('let them / may God judge between us'); 'God has judged (rendered judgment)' = mø̀ndø-geveá (30:6, 31:42).
Used five times in gen031 (44, 48-51). Three parties add 'o yaq X-a, yaq Y' (13:8).

entries.source: וַיָּשֶׂם אֹתָהּ מַצֵּבָה / וַיְרִימֶהָ מַצֵּבָה (set up a stone as a pillar)
entries.value: <nandi> … sasa ndøwuab. Andé uk me me꞉wuáb.
words: set it up as a pillar
entries.note: 'stood it up like a post'. Reused verbatim in gen031:45 and 51 (qatewuab: I set up). Gen 35:14, 35:20 need it.

entries.source: H6440 פָּנִים (face, countenance; 'his face was not toward him')
entries.value: bugug (face): Leiben-qá bugug ndøqeív (he saw Laban's face)
entries.note: Cain's fallen face (4:5-6) is bugug; 31:2 and 31:5 'his attitude had changed' = 'his face was not good to me, as before' (eqeieqei mbaín, av bugukhokhof ndægo), built.
Genesis writes the English loan (feature numerals.g); the NT writes the digits.
'the night that was' (19:34); gen031:29, 42.

entries.value: zeo (grandson: Nao-ge zeo); grandchildren of Laban = 'nogi nakhei mbasi neka tigi nakheis' (my daughters and their children)
entries.note: No plural of zeo found; gen031:28 says 'their children'.

entries.value: vimbum- (gèvimbumém they seized; toqo-vimbumem you would seize)
entries.note: gen031:31 'lest you take your daughters from me by force' = Soqaín ndøgo, … toqo-vimbumem.

entries.value: pizum- (Nandi vø̀pizømém! gather stones; vø̄pizumem they gathered)
entries.note: Things gathered; people assembling is pind- / møvab-.

entries.source: H2664 חָפַשׂ / H4959 מִשֵּׁשׁ (search, feel through)
entries.value: vawa- (look for): ndøvawát (he searched), qoqo-vawat (you searched)
entries.note: gen031:34-37; Gen 44:12 (the steward searched) needs it. Not found: qeiviáv (did not find, LUK 24:3).

entries.source: וַיִּקְרָא לְאֶחָיו לֶאֱכָל־לָחֶם (invited them to eat)
entries.note: Laban's wedding feast (29:22); gen031:54.
'slept one night' (24:54); alone ge-buv (28:11).

entries.source: H2721 חֹרֶב / H7140 קֶרַח (heat, cold, frost)
entries.note: gen031:40 'heat by day, frost by night' = Paveat-te, khøuwa tatas-qape … lova-te, qozaq …

entries.source: H5348 / H6124 / H1261 נָקֹד עָקֹד בָּרֹד (speckled, streaked, mottled)
entries.value: løvugiap (speckled), bokhotap-us (streaked, spotted), khagi papaqa-qasis (with white on the body, mottled)
entries.note: Genesis 30 has only two colour words for three Hebrew ones; gen031:8-12 gives the third as 'with white on it' (30:35). Question for the team.

entries.value: gita (harp, lyre); ouv (song): ouv neka gita namba
entries.note: Gen 4:21 has gita and pøinda (flute). Tambourine: gap:tambourine.g.

entries.value: Gilead (Gilead manqei popotap, the hill country of Gilead)
entries.note: Not in the corpus; kept as spelled (no r, no h; vowels close to the spelling). Place class noun for hill country as GEN 12:8, LUK 1:39.
Built: the double vowel written single like double consonants. Meaning in brackets (Khakhatap nandí, 'sign stones').
Built by the letter rules: j → z, final r drops, inner h drops, th → t. Marked '(Alam manqat-te.)' (in Aramaic) after Iblu manqat-te (GEN 29:32 note).
Built: final -ah → -a (letter rule). Meaning in brackets: Kewagam manqei (watching place).

entries.source: H3409 יָרֵךְ / כַּף הַיָּרֵךְ (thigh, hip, socket of the hip)
entries.note: Abraham's 'under my thigh' (24:2, 24:9); bov alone is leg (REV 10:1). gen032:26, 32, 33 use it for the hip and its socket.

'his legs were crippled' (ACT 14:8); the lame man is kagi ezoqam (ACT 3:2). gen032:32 'he was limping because of his hip' = 'bov gèmbo-wauwauám, teqa bov zapazapa zapaya'; gen032:26 also renders 'dislocated' with it (gap:dislocate.g).

nøfeap = fight, oppose; 'as they wrestled' = 'ndigu ginøfeapam ndøgo'. Rachel's wrestling (GEN 30:8, a different Hebrew word) is fifingiap (compete, 1CO 9:25); we kept nøfeap for a bodily fight. 2sg past 'qoqo-nøfeap' (gen032:29) is built on qoqo- (feature second_person_past).

entries.value: kopømba-én (won); 'could not overpower him' = kopømba mbaín, … tetømbuatat
entries.note: Rachel's 'I have won' (30:8) = mø̀e-kopømba-én; gen032:29 'you have prevailed' = mòqo-kopømba-én (2sg built). Overcome = tømbu- (1JN 2:13 mòzo-tømbuinám, 5:5 tetømbuatat).
'Lord, help me!' (MAT 15:25); a future 'he will rescue me' = 'no gékhandí꞉n' (2TI 4:18). 'from the hand of X' = 'X-qa zenda-te'.

No word for a camp in the corpus (the NT's 'camp' in HEB 13:11-13 is 'outside the town'). gen032 renders a group of people and animals as bawan and Mahanaim's meaning as 'Bawan menás'. Question for the team.

qatøz- (set apart, separate: Abraham's seven lambs 21:28) for dividing people and flocks, then the parts: 'bawan menás' (as 'Møvøyap foá', four parts, JHN 19:23). Also used for 'selected (a gift)' in gen032:14.
The same Hebrew word as Cain's and Abel's offering (4:3-5). Jacob's gift to Esau (32:14-22, 33:10) = etoam matev; 'to give to Esau' = 'Isao-te etoam matev nonqo'.

entries.source: female / male animals (עִזִּים / תְּיָשִׁים, רְחֵלִים / אֵילִים, פָּרוֹת / פָּרִים, אֲתֹנֹת / עְיָרִם)
entries.note: The team marks sex with angana / sakheis after the animal (30:35, 12:16; ewe lambs 21:28). One ram = sip anganeam (22:13); a heifer = kao-yu (HEB 9:13). Milk camels: 'kemol sakheis … tiqa nakheis namba' (gap:milk_camels.g).

entries.source: H6413 פְּלֵיטָה (escape, the remnant that escapes)
entries.note: 'they will not escape' (1TH 5:3) turned positive for gen032:9; flee = khokhon (term:H1272).

entries.source: H3190 הֵיטִיב עִם (do good to, make prosper)
entries.value: matev eqeieqei nøtaqá-matanám (I will do good to you)
entries.note: God's promise 'I will do good to you' on the pattern of 28:14 (nøzǿ- I to them → nøtaqá- I to you sg, as 13:16 nøtaqá-etoám). gen032:10, 13.

entries.source: H7725 שׁוּב (imperative: go back, return to your land)
entries.note: 'to the ground you will return' (3:19). gen031:3 and 31:13 wrote 'nango mòqoveséz', a form not found in the corpus; gen032:10 uses qonǿveséz. A later revision of gen031 may follow.
Isaac touching Jacob (27:22); used for the man touching Jacob's hip (gen032:26, 33).
kinik = ligament (COL 2:19, EPH 4:16, only 2 verses). gen032:33 'the tendon on the hip' = 'søvakha gigiap-qa kinik ndøgo, bov zapazapa-te nqøugu'.
'trouble and distress will come upon them' (ROM 2:9) with fakhan + mbo- (came to him, 31:24).

entries.source: קָטֹנְתִּי מִכֹּל הַחֲסָדִים (I am unworthy of all the kindness)
entries.note: The Hebrew says 'I am small': Ruth's self-abasement (formula:humble_self) fits word for word. Then the kindness: 'Qo kuku matev … qoqonøgo' (RUT 2:10 pattern).

entries.source: אֲכַפְּרָה פָנָיו (I will appease him, lit. cover his face)
entries.note: 'until your brother's anger subsides' (27:44, of the same Esau).

entries.source: יִשָּׂא פָנָי (he will accept me, lift up my face)
entries.note: 'someone will be kind to me' (RUT 2:2) + perhaps (formula:perhaps).

entries.source: שַׁלְּחֵנִי (let me go, send me away)
entries.note: Jacob to Laban (30:25). 'I will not let you go' = 'No qo nótakák' (gen032:27, built on gembótakák, 1CO 10:13, and nó-…-ák).

entries.source: לָמָּה זֶּה תִּשְׁאַל לִשְׁמִי (Why do you ask my name?)
entries.note: Jesus's 'Why do you ask me about what is good?' (MAT 19:17).

entries.source: לֹא <X> יֵאָמֵר עוֹד שִׁמְךָ כִּי אִם־<Y> (your name will no longer be X but Y)
entries.value: Qoqa iz, <X> sekemba gégoák. Geté <Y> qágoát.
words: your name will no longer be
entries.note: Abram → Abraham (17:5), with the meaning in brackets. Gen 32:29 and 35:10 (Jacob → Israel).
Isaac's well (26:33), with 'therefore'.
Also GEN 16:8 'av khoqotéma?' (Hagar).

entries.source: וַאֲמַרְתֶּם / תְּדַבְּרוּן אֶל (you pl are to say to him)
entries.value: āv qazømbøé-einím nqǽgo, ‘…’; 'tell him the same' = manqat kopó vømømbó-einīm
entries.note: The disciples' instruction (MAT 21:3, LUK 19:31: if anyone asks …, say …). 2sg built in gen032:19: 'āv qombøé-eín nqǽgo'.
Jesus left alone with the woman (JHN 8:9).
MRK 4:6, MAT 13:6.

entries.source: וַיִּשְׁלַח מַלְאָכִים לְפָנָיו (sent messengers ahead of him)
entries.note: Human messengers are u-anim (sg u-anem), not enzol ezoqam (angels). 'the messengers returned' = 'u-anim … giqavaz' (LUK 7:10).
Not in the corpus; inner h drops (letter rule), the vowels kept. Meaning in brackets: 'Bawan menás' (two groups).
j → z, double consonant single; river class noun kea (place_class_noun).
Not in the corpus; kept as spelled (both forms, as the Hebrew). Meaning in brackets: 'Mbumbukiam-qa bugug' (the face of God).

entries.source: וַיִּפְצַר־בּוֹ (he urged him, pressed him; insisted)
entries.note: Lot urging the angels (19:3, to them: gèzø-); to one person gèmbo- is built on the gembo-/gezø- pair. gen033:11.

entries.source: קַח / וְלָקַחְתָּ (take, accept a gift) ; וַיִּקָּח (and he took it)
entries.value: sègekhatiú (accept it, imperative); he took it = ndøndaf
entries.note: Abraham to Ephron 'accept my price' (23:13). 'X took it' after urging: 'X até gendego, … ndøndaf' (gen033:11).
Lot's refusal to the angels (19:3), a polite 'not so'. gen033:10.

entries.source: יְהִי לְךָ אֲשֶׁר־לָךְ (keep what is yours)
entries.value: Qoqa gigiap, bètaqagó. (let your goods be yours)
entries.note: 14:21 'take the goods for yourself' = '… bètaqagó' (may it be yours). gen033:9.

entries.value: tanakh + go: Mbumbukiam no tanakh genøgo (God had mercy on me)
entries.note: The NT's 'have mercy on me' (tanakh gènøgó, imperative) and 'God had mercy on him' (tanakh mbogó); the 3sg past with nø- (me) is built. Same word as favour (term:H2580). gen033:5, 11.

entries.source: רִאשֹׁנָה / אַחֲרֹנִים (first, next, last; in front, at the rear)
entries.value: bugukhokhof (first) … Taqa zita-te (after that) … Yaq vaev-te (last of all)
entries.note: Order of a line of people (gen033:2) and 'and then Joseph and Rachel' (33:7).

entries.value: ginduzáv (they came, pl); he came near = gèkhanøgím; near X = X avønin-te
entries.note: gen033:6-7 'X avønin-te ginduzáv'.

entries.value: ekeza kha, manqei me꞉laém (they threw themselves to the ground)
entries.note: Plural of 'ekeza kha, manqei me꞉laváo. Bugug até manqei-té.' (GEN 17:3); the singular formula is formula:bowed_down.g. gen033:6-7.

entries.value: kha bazaføgakh mbaín (the body has no strength)

entries.note: 'another dream' = 'venanqei nøme'. The 1sg qate-tamat (after qate-manqatam) and 2sg qoqo-tamat (second_person_past) are built. gen037:5-10.

A sheep falling 'into a pit' (MAT 12:11); REV 9:1 the Abyss is 'manqei ozu vaev mbain' (pit without end). 'throw him into a pit' = 'manqei ozu-té ginø-oginám' (REV 20:15 'ginø-oginám'). After the first mention gen037 says 'ta ozu'.

entries.source: מָשַׁךְ / הֶעֱלָה מִן־הַבּוֹר (pull up, lift out of the pit)
entries.note: The man lifts his sheep out of the pit (MAT 12:11); God raised Jonah from the pit (JON 2:7). The chain form vø̄livav is built (imperative_chain). gen037:28.

entries.source: חַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ (a vicious animal has devoured him)
entries.value: søvakha gigiap lozokhak soqøsoqa, pakhapakha mbokhanøém, kha vø̄log
entries.note: 'wild animals killed him and ate his body': lozokhak = wild, soqøsoqa = bad; the verbs plural as REV 17:16 (the beast and the horns eat her flesh). gen037:20, 33; also 44:28.

entries.source: יִשְׁמְעֵאלִים (the Ishmaelites; a caravan of Ishmaelites)

Not in the corpus. th → t (letter rule); a town takes taon (place_class_noun). gen037:17.
Not in the corpus. ph → f, a final r drops (Tama, Asa). gen037:36; 39:1.

entries.source: מְדָנִים (the Medanites, Gen 37:36 Hebrew; the BSB has Midianites)
entries.note: Medan, Abraham's son, is in the team's 25:2. The Hebrew of 37:36 has הַמְּדָנִים (Medanites), the BSB 'Midianites' (as 37:28 and 39:1); the draft follows the Hebrew and the notes give the BSB form.
The merchants of the earth (REV 18). 'Midianite traders' = 'Midian bawan bisnis ezoqam'. gen037:28.

entries.source: סְרִיס (officer, official, eunuch of a king)
entries.note: The Ethiopian eunuch, the queen's court official (ACT 8:27-39). 'an officer of Pharaoh' = 'Felo-ge gaman ezoqam'. gen037:36; 39:1; 40:2.

entries.value: vos keoge ezoqam-ge kawa (the chief of the guards)
entries.note: The captain of the temple guard (ACT 4:1, 5:24) without 'temple': 'Felo-gi vos keoge ezoqam-ge kawa'. gen037:36; 39:1; 40:3-4.

entries.source: וַיַּעַבְרוּ (they passed by, were passing on the road)
entries.note: 'while they were on the road' (the lepers on their way). gen037:28.
In Joseph's dream the grain is wit (term:H2406); 1pl past 'qati-abap' is built. 'My sheaf stood upright' = 'gè-itán. Andé uk me me꞉wuáb' (GEN 28:18 the stone set up). gen037:7.

entries.source: וַיִּשְׂנְאוּ אֹתוֹ / וַיּוֹסִפוּ עוֹד שְׂנֹא אֹתוֹ (they hated him; hated him even more)
entries.value: gèmbo-sanqaupám; even more = nøme mba gèmbo-sanqaupám

entries.source: וַיְקַנְאוּ בוֹ (they were jealous of him)
entries.note: The NT's own words for Joseph's brothers (ACT 7:9). gen037:11.

entries.source: שָׁמַר אֶת־הַדָּבָר (kept the matter in mind)
entries.note: Mary treasured these things (LUK 2:19, 2:51). gen037:11.

entries.value: <Y> ate gi꞉goam mokho-te, poev kandambaqape, <X>-té qambogoám
entries.note: Jacob's love for Rachel above Leah (29:30). gen037:3-4.

'our brother Sosthenes'. The kin noun eveqase has the possessor in its stem (e- his, qa- your, zø- your pl); no 1pl form was found, so gen037:26-27 use nøfu. 'he is our own flesh' = 29:14 in the 1pl: 'Ndego unimanqatin nigí nøfú. Uni-nikeza-kouk-ín.' (GEN 29:14 'Uni-nøkeza-kouk-ín'). Question for the Kuni team.

entries.source: כִּי־אָחִינוּ בְשָׂרֵנוּ הוּא (for he is our brother, our own flesh)
entries.note: Laban's words to Jacob in the 1pl (nikeza, reflexive_possessive). gen037:27.

entries.source: וַיִּקְרַע אֶת־בְּגָדָיו / שִׂמְלֹתָיו (he tore his clothes)
entries.note: The high priest (MRK 14:63); plural 'ekeza ndabua ndøkeqagím' (ACT 14:14). gen037:29, 34; 44:13.

entries.source: וַיָּשֶׂם שַׂק בְּמָתְנָיו (put sackcloth around his waist)
entries.note: Jesus tying the towel round his waist (JHN 13:4); sackcloth = bad clothes (term:H8242). gen037:34.

entries.source: וַיָּקֻמוּ … לְנַחֲמוֹ וַיְמָאֵן לְהִתְנַחֵם (they tried to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted)
entries.value: teqa mokho khakheinam-qa ndøgoám. Geté ndego poeveáv.
entries.note: Rachel 'refusing to be comforted' = no one could set right their insides (MAT 2:18); 'tried to' = purpose -qa ndøgoám (ACT 7:26). gen037:35.

entries.source: אֵרֵד … שְׁאֹלָה (I will go down to Sheol, mourning)
entries.value: … mutøkhop neka eiv matev ndæ̀goát, atema nǿnaním
entries.note: Sheol as 'until I die' (term:H7585 løvøte avønin-te is 'close to death', JON 2:3). 'I will go to my son' = 'noge yo-te ndæ̀náv' (JHN 8:21 'No ndæ̀náv'). gen037:35; 42:38, 44:29-31 need it.

entries.source: נְכֹאת וּצְרִי וָלֹט (spices, balm and myrrh)
entries.value: gigiap sisip mbomømboma neka tae et neka mel tae et
entries.note: The magi's gifts (MAT 2:11; mel = myrrh, glossary). balm has no word: 'tae et' (tree oil) is built. gen037:25; 43:11.
upøgim = carry, pick up (MRK 16:18; GEN 14:11 carried off). gen037:25.
Hagar wandering in the wilderness (21:14); gu꞉- is the durative (verb_subject_prefix.2), not feminine, so it stands for Joseph too. gen037:15.

entries.source: נָסְעוּ מִזֶּה (they have moved on from here)
entries.note: 'left that place' (MAT 12:9); perfective mø̀ndø-. gen037:17.

entries.source: רְאֵה אֶת־שְׁלוֹם אַחֶיךָ (see how your brothers are faring)
entries.note: Paul's 'let us visit the brothers, to see how they are' (ACT 15:36); the 2sg qomǿ-zømét is built from zimǿ-zømét. gen037:14.

וַיִּתְנַכְּלוּ אֹתוֹ לַהֲמִיתוֹ (they plotted to kill him)
entries.note: The council's plot against Jesus (JHN 11:53). gen037:18.

entries.source: וַיִּרְאוּ אֹתוֹ מֵרָחֹק (they saw him in the distance)
entries.note: MRK 5:6; 'before he reached them' = 'ti-te fakhaneav ndøgoám' (JHN 11:30). gen037:18.

entries.source: מַה־בֶּצַע כִּי … (what profit is it if …)
entries.note: 'how does it help me / him' (1CO 15:32, LUK 9:25), here with the 1pl object (khanimbé-, built). gen037:26.

entries.source: וַיִּמְכְּרוּ … בְּעֶשְׂרִים כָּסֶף (sold him for twenty pieces of silver)
entries.value: <seller> <X>, <buyer>-te gèwiím. Fia ndøgo, silva moni mokho <N>.
entries.note: The price as its own sentence (23:15). gen037:28, 36.
Isaac feeling Jacob (27:21). gen037:32.
2sg imperative of qeiv (see) as in gen031:12; 'we found this' = 'Nqanek qatiqeiví' (1pl, 26:28). 'he recognized it' = gèmatøvém (built on gimatøvemem, ACT 3:10). gen037:32-33.

entries.source: אַל־תִּשְׁפְּכוּ־דָם … וְיָד אַל־תִּשְׁלְחוּ־בוֹ (do not shed blood; do not lay a hand on him, pl)
entries.value: Zo ndego pakhapakha mbokhanø̀e᷄m … Geté ndego, matev nøme mbomatønòme᷄m.
entries.note: Plural prohibitives built on the pattern of RUT 2:15 (prohibitive.3); 'let us not take his life' = 'Ndego pakhapakha bizi-làe᷄m' (1pl as GAL 5:26 'bizi-khambùva᷄p'), 'let us not lay a hand' = 'matev nøme bizi-matønòme᷄m'. 'shed blood' = kill (image_to_meaning). gen037:21-22, 27.

entries.source: וְכִסִּינוּ אֶת־דָּמוֹ (and cover up his blood)
entries.note: khonab = hide (MAT 25:25; gen035:4), 1pl zí- built. gen037:26.
As the Valley of Gerar (26:17). gen037:14.

entries.source: הֲמָלֹךְ תִּמְלֹךְ עָלֵינוּ אִם־מָשׁוֹל תִּמְשֹׁל בָּנוּ (do you intend to reign over us, will you actually rule us?)
entries.value: Gê, qo nigi kawa ezoqam qógoât? Gê, qo ni qonimbó-kawaevât?
entries.note: The doubling of the Hebrew verb is rendered by two questions; qógoât (2sg future of go 'be', 27:39 qógoák) and qonimbó-kawaevât (built on 27:40 with 2sg qo- and 1pl ni-) are not attested as such. gen037:8.
Luke 3:28-29 writes the ancestor Er as E (final r drops, as Eba for Eber). gen038:3, 6-7; 46:12.
Not in the corpus; kept as spelt (no letter rule applies). gen038:4, 8-10; 46:12.

entries.value: Sua (Sua-gu yu, the daughter of Shua)
entries.note: Not in the corpus. sh → s (letter rule, Tasis). The Hebrew 38:2 lets 'his name' refer to the man (BSB); 38:12 'bat-Shua' = 'Sua-gu yu'. gen038:2, 12.
Not in the corpus. Initial h kept as in Genesis names (Hiblon, Hit), r → l, final h drops. gen038:1, 12.
Double consonants single; origin suffix -ak (suffix_origin). gen038:1, 12, 20.
Not in the corpus. ch → k; a small place takes vemiav (place_class_noun). gen038:5.
Final h drops (as the chief Timna, gen036). Gen 38:12-14.

entries.value: Enaim (Enaim vemiav mboqog tambav-te, at the gate of Enaim)
entries.note: Not in the corpus. 'Entrance' as the village gate (RUT 4:1). gen038:14, 21.

entries.value: zimui (Kayafas-gé zimuí); your = qoge zimui (built), her = tuge zimui
entries.note: One NT model, a man's father-in-law. Kin nouns may change their stem with the possessor's person (zakhapuka/qakhapuka, ziwap/qæwap): the 2nd-person form is unknown. Question for the Kuni team. gen038:13, 25.
Kin form with -pakha and the 2nd-person stem qæwap (feature kin_pakha). gen038:11, 16, 24.
The angel's 'seal of the living God' (REV 7:2). 'put a seal on' = 'mbusa ndømøpá' (JHN 6:27, 2CO 1:22). gen038:18, 25; 41:42 needs it.
khakhatap = sign; the Spirit 'as a pledge' (2CO 5:5). gen038:17-18, 20.

entries.value: mevoat; the scarlet thread = mevoat køkouk
entries.note: One model: Abram will not take 'even a thread' (14:23). Red = køkouk (gap:colours). gen038:18, 25, 28, 30.
The BSB's 'items' (the pledge) are 'gigiap ndigu' (those things), 'nginik gigiap' (these things). gen038:20, 23, 25-26.
zifu / zifuap (JHN 15:13); the address 'friend!' is Khanánqa (term:H7453friend.h). tege zifu (his) is built on the possessive series. gen038:12, 20.
'there were twins in her womb' (25:24). gen038:27.
Young goats in the plural = naningus nakheis (27:9, 27:16). gen038:17, 20, 23.

entries.value: <X> gumu-khouwev (grew up); 'until X grows up' = 'atema <X> vumúfīs'
entries.note: Also 'mø̀ndømu-khouwév' (has grown, 2×), HEB 11:24, RUT 4:17. gen038:11, 14.

entries.source: הֵסִיר / לָבַשׁ בִּגְדֵי (take off / put on garments)
entries.value: ndabua ge-uzupam, gekhòfoē (took off the clothes he wore); put on = ndabua vø̄-uzam
entries.note: Feminine gu-uzupam, gukhòfoē (built, gu- for she). 'widow's garments' = 'tuqa ngæmam ndabua' (built). gen038:14, 19.

entries.source: וַתְּכַס בַּצָּעִיף וַתִּתְעַלָּף (covered herself with a veil)
entries.note: Rebekah's veil (24:65). 'because she had covered her face' = 'ndugu bugug mø̀ndø-khonáo' (built perfective); the veil as a thing = 'ndabua bugug khonao nonqo' (built). gen038:14-15, 19.
Said of the woman caught in adultery (JHN 8:3); of men 'mambe mé꞉wáv' (LUK 16:18). 'pregnant from it' = 'kha viniv-ús, mambe matev-te'. gen038:24.
No word for a temple prostitute; the same word as זוֹנָה (term for prostitute, gen034:31), so Hirah's word and Judah's thought (38:15) stay one. gen038:21-22.

entries.value: gøinam-te <...>-nqagim (throw into the fire); 'fire burns her' = gøinám guní-lonqotøvém
entries.note: Judah's order 'Bring her out! Let her be burned' = 'Ndugu bavokho zó-itú. Gøinam-te vø̄-nqagimém!' (2pl commands built: zó- + itu, chain vø̄-). gen038:24.

entries.source: פֶּן נִהְיֶה לָבוּז (lest we become a laughingstock)
entries.value: Soqaín ndøgo, ezoqa ewaqape ni gévøngi꞉namát
entries.note: LUK 14:29 (everyone will ridicule him); the object ni (us) as a free pronoun. gen038:23.
Also JHN 9:12 'Gê, ndego ndakin kenáqape?'. gen038:21.

words: no shrine prostitute has been here

entries.note: Pilate's 'let it be given to him' (MAT 27:58). gen038:23.

entries.note: MAT 26:15 is plural (you pl give me); the 2sg qonǿ- is built. gen038:16.
The servant's polite request (24:17, 24:43). 'let me sleep with you' = 'Kopømbâ, no qo namba tæ-sømbi?' with sømbi as GEN 30:15. gen038:16.

entries.source: וְלֹא־יָסַף עוֹד לְדַעְתָּהּ (he did not know her again)
entries.note: The negative of formula 'venanqei nonqo vø̄tøkuanem'. gen038:26.

entries.value: patu <...>-qatayat (raise children for the dead brother)
entries.note: The NT tells the levirate law (MRK 12:19). Judah's order: 'Qaveqase-gu zas mòqokható (24:51). … neka qaveqase-te, patu vømbō-qatayat' (chain built). gen038:8-9.
Mary stayed about three months (LUK 1:56). gen038:24.
Abraham was told (22:20); used for a woman too (a plural subject wins, verb_subject_prefix.2). gen038:13, 24.
The newborn's arm; 'on his wrist' = 'teqa pingim-te' (ACT 12:7). gen038:28.
Peter's chains fastened on his wrists (ACT 12:7); the chain form vø̄løvøtup is built. gen038:28, 30.

entries.source: צָדְקָה מִמֶּנִּי (she is more righteous than I)
entries.note: Comparative 'A, B mø̀ndøløvú' (feature comparative) after the plain statement; feminine -qapú as kandambaqapu (REV 19:2). gen038:26.
Agent noun (feature agent_noun) on term H1494 (su qogem-, shear). gen038:12.

entries.value: mokho qafakhan (it came to fruit, it succeeded); "the LORD made all he did succeed" = "matev ate ndægo, ndego gematanam, Evezøza ndego gembo-tøke, yaq mokho qafakhan"
entries.note: The servant's journey made successful (24:21, 24:40, 24:56: "Evezøza, mø̀ndønø-tøké … mokho mø̀ndøfakhán"). gembo-tøke (helped him) is built on 24:56. gen039:2, 3, 23; 24:40.

entries.source: וַיְהִי יְהוָה אֶת־<X> (the LORD was with X)
entries.note: God was with the boy (21:20). A nominal clause "the LORD is with him" (39:3, 23) = "Evezøza ndøgoám, te namba" / "mø̀ndøgoám". gen039:2, 3, 21, 23.

entries.value: otøotam vewe- (make fun of): "ni otøotam vewe-qa" (to mock us)
entries.note: Ishmael mocking Isaac (21:9, the same Hebrew verb). The purpose form vewe-qa (feature suffix_purpose) is built. gen039:14, 17.

entries.source: קָרָא בְּקוֹל גָּדוֹל / הֵרִים קוֹל (cry out, scream, raise the voice)
entries.value: qæ-akhá (I cried out); "noqa akhayam" (my crying); loudly = "manqat bazaføgakh-ús"
entries.note: Jonah's "you heard my voice" = "noqa akhayam mòqo-ewág" (JON 2:3); a loud call = "with strong words" (ACT 14:10). gen039:14, 15, 18.

entries.value: geagim (grab, hold): "the men grabbed his hand" = "pingi vøzø̄geagim"; she grabbed him by his cloak = "Zosef-qa ndabua gu-geagim" (built)
entries.note: gu-geagim (she grabbed) is built with gu- (verb_subject_prefix.2). gen039:12.

entries.value: keaeqateáv (did not withhold): "ndego gigiap-qase keaeqateáv, no-te"
entries.note: Abraham did not withhold his son (22:12, 22:16); the same form for 3sg in gen039:9.

entries.source: יְפֵה־תֹאַר וִיפֵה מַרְאֶה (handsome in form and appearance)
entries.value: <X>, ndego bugug keogé. Qanimáv tentév. (he looked fine; he was very good)
entries.note: Rachel shapely and beautiful (29:17, the same Hebrew pair) with the masculine tentév (attested 2×) for tuntúv. gen039:6.

entries.source: לֹא־יָדַע אִתּוֹ מְאוּמָה / אֵין רֹאֶה אֶת־כָּל־מְאוּמָה (he did not concern himself with anything)
entries.value: <X> gigiap-qase otevateáv (he knew nothing at all)
entries.note: gigiap-qase + negative verb = nothing (ACT 11:8, ACT 23:14); otevateáv (did not know, 24×). The warden's "did not see to anything" (39:23) takes the same wording. gen039:6, 8, 23.

entries.source: וַיָּנָס וַיֵּצֵא הַחוּצָה (he fled and ran outside)
entries.value: gèbǿin, bavokhó genøfakhán (he ran, he went out outside)
entries.note: ACT 19:16 the men ran out of the house; flee from a person = khokhon (16:6). genøfakhán (9× genøfakhan) with the tones of the model verbs. gen039:12, 13, 15, 18.

entries.source: וַיֵּט אֵלָיו חֶסֶד (the LORD showed him kindness)
entries.value: Teqa kuku matev, <X>-te kandambá. (his kindness to X was great)
entries.note: God's loving devotion = kuku matev (gap:loving_devotion); the servant's "his kindness to my master" (24:27). gen039:21.

entries.source: מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי <X> / נָתַן חִנּוֹ בְּעֵינֵי <X> (find favour in X's eyes)
entries.value: <X>, <Y> tanakh mbogó (X was kind to Y)
entries.note: The subject turns: the one in whose eyes favour is found is kind to the other (Julius kind to Paul, ACT 27:3); term:H2580 (tanakh). God giving the favour = "Evezøza <Y> gembo-tøke, yaq …" (built). gen039:4, 21.

entries.source: נָתַן / עָזַב בְּיַד <X> (put / leave in X's hand, entrust to X)
entries.value: gigiap ate qambøegoam, <X>-qá zenda-té genø-vé (gave) / genø-iváv (left)
entries.note: Abraham gave / left everything he owned to Isaac (24:36, 25:5). gen039:4, 6, 8, 22.

entries.source: הִפְקִיד עַל (put in charge of, make overseer)
entries.value: <X>, teqa khoev-te keoge ezoqam ndøvé (made him keeper of his house)
entries.note: "I have made him master" (27:37) and "he will make him keeper" (LUK 12:44) with the narrative past ndøvé (16×). gen039:4, 5; 41:41.

entries.value: tege sasae ezoqam ndøgoám, te avønin-te (he was his servant, near him)
entries.note: No word for a personal attendant; "servant near him" built. gen039:4; 40:4.
The Philippian jailer. Prisoners = ndimbula ezoqa (ACT 16:25); the king's prisoners = kawa ezoqam-gi ndimbula ezoqa. gen039:21-23; 40:3.

entries.source: וַיִּתְּנֵהוּ אֶל־בֵּית הַסֹּהַר (put him in prison)
entries.note: "was kept in prison" = "ndimbula mokho-te ge-utavam" (ACT 12:5), a model for "where the prisoners were confined" (gen039 wrote "gi꞉goam", were there). gen039:20; 40:3, 15; 41:10.
"living among them day after day" (2PE 2:8); "although … he refused" = two sentences joined by Geté. gen039:10.

entries.value: manqa-zapa tægo, Mbumbukiam-qa bøi-te (that I sin in God's eyes)
entries.note: God to Abimelech: "so that you would not sin against me" (20:6). The question "how could I …?" = "Gê, no kopømbâ, … tæ-…? Āv taoká." (ability + interjection, built). gen039:9.
The same BSB words. "refused to (do)" with a following verb = poeveáv + irrealis (LUK 15:28, gen039:10). gen039:8; 48:19.

entries.value: waen etoam ezoqam (wine-giving man); the chief one = waen etoam ezoqam kandambaqape
entries.note: No cupbearer in the corpus (searched cupbearer|master of the banquet|wine steward: only JHN 2:8-9 'lou loge megeat ezoqam', the banquet master). Agent noun (feature agent_noun) on the waterer of 1CO 3:8; a single chief as the high priest 'iziz ezoqam kandambaqape' (ACT 5:17), so that kawa (head, also chief) stays free for 'lift up the head'. gen040 names them 'kandambaqape' once (40:2) and then by the plain title, as the BSB's 'the cupbearer'. Gen 41:9 needs it.

entries.source: אֹפֶה / שַׂר הָאֹפִים (baker; chief baker); מַעֲשֵׂה אֹפֶה (baked goods)
entries.value: flawa løvusam ezoqam (bread-baking man); chief = flawa løvusam ezoqam kandambaqape; baked goods = 'lou … flawa løvusam ezoqam gi꞉løvusumatun' (food the bakers bake)
entries.note: løvus- = bake bread (Lot 19:3, Sarah 18:6) and roast offerings (8:20 'søvakha gigiap løvusam nonqo'); agent noun as term:cupbearer.g. Gen 41:10 needs it.
The twelve baskets of leftovers (JHN 6:13, LUK 9:17) and the basket over a lamp. Paul's basket down the wall is ava (bag, 2CO 11:33). gen040:16-18.

entries.source: כּוֹס (cup, Pharaoh's cup; Joseph's silver cup)
entries.note: The loan kap (cup and dish). The 'cup' of suffering is ibøkha khaqain-qape (JHN 18:11), not this. gen040:11, 13, 21; 44:2-17 (the silver cup: silva kap, by rule).

entries.value: waen tae (vine); waen tae nanga (grapes, clusters); branches = tang
entries.note: The fruit of the vine (LUK 22:18, MAT 26:29), the grapes of the earth (REV 14:18-19). gen040:9-11; 49:11 needs it.

entries.value: mbusa qafakhan (buds came out); flawas (flowers); qakhatøkhatoam (it is ripe)
entries.note: Aaron's staff that budded (HEB 9:4), the flower of the field (JAS 1:10-11, the loan flawas), the harvest that is ripe (MAT 9:37, LUK 10:2). Put together in gen040:10.
Only the noun 'pressing thing' (winepress) is attested; the verb is built from it. A question for the team. gen040:11.

entries.source: מַדּוּעַ פְּנֵיכֶם רָעִים / זֹעֲפִים (why are your faces downcast; distraught)
entries.value: Gekha zapâ, … bugug avus-mba ndozote-keoge? (why do you look with a fallen face, pl); distraught = mbøni ndøzøvaev (their hearts are sad)
words: why are your faces so downcast
entries.note: Cain's fallen face (4:5-6) is the team's model; the 2pl ndozote- is built on ndoqote- (2sg) and ndozo- (ndozo-matavap). gen040:6-7; Neh 2:2.

entries.value: <X> ge꞉qan, ta khøuwa iz gemø-khantaz (the day of his birth came)
entries.note: Herod's birthday banquet (MRK 6:21). gen040:20.

entries.note: Abraham's feast for Isaac (21:8) and Herod's banquet 'with his nobles' (MRK 6:21, guests with namba). gen040:20; 43:16-34.

entries.source: זָכַר / שָׁכַח (remember, remember me; not remember; forget)
entries.value: remember me = No gènøndo-matøvém; did not remember = <X> matavapøteáv; forgot him = teqa yaq-te, manqa mate mø̀ndømbøe-navøém
entries.note: The thief's 'remember me when you come into your kingdom' (LUK 23:42) fits 40:14 word for word. 'God remembered Noah' = 'God's memory did not end' (8:1): manqa mate + navøem is forgetting. gen040:14, 23; 41:9, 41:30, 41:51.

entries.value: This is its interpretation = 'Taqa manqa mokho nqánek:'; no one to interpret = 'ezoqa nøme mbaín, taqa manqa mokho tenømand'; as Joseph interpreted = 'av Zosef venanqei-qa manqa mokho gezø-ein ndægo'
entries.note: Applies gap:interpret_dream.g as it proposes (the gap stays open as the team's question). 'the interpretation was favorable' = 'Zosef-qa manqa mokho ndøgo, qanimáv' (on 1:4 'āv geneqeív nqǽgo, … qanimáv'). 'Don't interpretations belong to God?' = 'Gê, venanqei-qa manqa mokho, Mbumbukiam-qâ mbà?' (rhetorical_question, built). gen040:5, 8, 12, 16, 18, 22; 41.
The temple raised in three days. gen040:13, 19.

entries.source: יִשָּׂא אֶת־רֹאשְׁךָ (lift up your head: restore); יִשָּׂא אֶת־רֹאשְׁךָ מֵעָלֶיךָ (lift your head off you: behead)
entries.value: restore = 'qo kawa ndø̀qa-eqá' (he will lift your head); behead = 'qo monqo ndø̀qa-kepáz' (he will cut your neck); 'lifted up the heads of A and B' = 'A-qa kawa ndø-eqá, neka B-qa kawa ndø-eqá'
entries.note: The Hebrew word play is kept in 40:13 and 20 with the attested 'lift up the head' (LUK 21:28, of hope); the baker's 'lift off your head' is told by its meaning, the NT's beheading of John (MRK 6:27). Future 3sg-on-you ndø̀qa- as 3:15. gen040:13, 19, 20.

entries.value: tae-té <…>-tøkew: genø-tøkéw (he hanged him), ndø̀qanø-tøkéw (he will hang you)
entries.note: Jesus hanged on a tree (ACT 5:30, 10:39; tae mutui is the cross). Plain tae (tree) for עֵץ. The 3sg forms are built on the 3pl ginø-tøkewém. Judas hanging himself is 'ekeza monqo møfók' (MAT 27:5). gen040:19, 22; 41:13.

entries.value: ezoqa nøme, no <place>-te ndøgo, gi-aqonømem (some people stole me from …)
entries.note: aqon- = steal (term:H1589.g); the passive is told with 'some people' as subject, as formula:was_told.g. The object marking of gi-aqonømem (14:16, of captives) is not certain. gen040:15.

entries.source: חָטָא לְ<X> (offend, sin against X); לֹא־עָשִׂיתִי מְאוּמָה (I have done nothing)
entries.value: <X>-te manqa-zapa gigonem (they did wrong to X); I have done nothing = no manqa-zapa-qase goneáv
entries.note: Paul's 'I have done nothing wrong to the Jews' (ACT 25:10). gen040:1, 15; 41:9 (my faults).

entries.note: ACT 1:20 'may another take his position' = teqa sasae; nqawa = again (MRK 8:25). gen040:13, 21; 41:13.

entries.source: וַיִּפְקֹד אֶת־<X> אִתָּם (assigned X to them)
entries.value: <X> ndøvé, ti namba (he put X with them)
entries.note: ndøvé (put, made, 16×) with the company phrase after the verb (constituent_order.2). The attendant is term:attendant.g in the plural (tige sasae ezoqam … ti avønin-te). gen040:4.
